description: Retron SMARTS pattern library. Each retron is a substructure in a target molecule that implies a specific retrosynthetic transform.

retrons.name: biaryl_suzuki
retrons.description: Biaryl C–C bond ← aryl/heteroaryl halide + arylboronic acid (Suzuki)
retrons.notes: Highly reliable. Works for electron-rich and electron-poor arenes. Pd/phosphine catalyst (SPhos, XPhos, dppf). Base: K2CO3, Cs2CO3, K3PO4. Prefer Br/I over Cl. Watch for protodeboronation of electron-poor boronic acids.

retrons.name: aryl_alkyl_negishi
retrons.description: Aryl–alkyl C–C bond ← aryl halide + alkylzinc (Negishi)
retrons.notes: Pd or Ni catalysis. Organozinc reagents are air-sensitive. β-hydride elimination can be a problem with primary alkyl chains.

retrons.name: aryl_alkene_heck
retrons.description: Aryl vinyl bond ← aryl halide + alkene (Heck/Mizoroki-Heck)
retrons.notes: Pd catalysis. E-selectivity usually preferred. Regioselectivity depends on alkene substitution. DMF or DMA solvent, tertiary amine base.

retrons.name: aryl_alkyne_sonogashira
retrons.description: Aryl–alkyne bond ← aryl halide + terminal alkyne (Sonogashira)
retrons.notes: Pd/Cu co-catalysis in amine solvent (Et3N, iPr2NH). Avoid Cu if alkyne dimerization (Glaser) is a concern. TMS-protected alkyne → deprotect after coupling.

retrons.name: beta_hydroxy_carbonyl_aldol
retrons.description: β-Hydroxy carbonyl ← aldehyde/ketone + enolizable carbonyl (Aldol)
retrons.notes: Classic C–C forming reaction. Mukaiyama aldol (TMS enol ether + Lewis acid) for stereocontrol. Intramolecular aldol for ring formation. Evans oxazolidinone auxiliaries for asymmetric.

retrons.name: alkene_wittig
retrons.description: Alkene ← carbonyl compound + phosphonium ylide (Wittig)
retrons.notes: Non-stabilized ylides give Z-alkene. Stabilized (ester, CN) give E. Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons (phosphonate ester) is E-selective and more reactive. Byproduct: Ph3P=O (add MgBr2 for HWE).

retrons.name: grignard_alcohol
retrons.description: Secondary/tertiary alcohol ← carbonyl + Grignard (RMgX)
retrons.notes: Anhydrous conditions. THF or Et2O solvent. Sensitive to moisture and air. Incompatible with acidic protons, esters (double addition), nitriles. Consider organolithium for hindered substrates.

retrons.name: alkyl_alkyl_kumada
retrons.description: Alkyl–alkyl C–C bond ← alkyl halide + alkyl Grignard (Kumada)
retrons.notes: Ni or Pd catalysis. Less common than Suzuki/Negishi. Grignard is an air-sensitive, basic reagent. Used for unfunctionalized alkyl couplings.

retrons.name: aryl_amine_buchwald
retrons.description: Aryl amine ← aryl halide/triflate + amine (Buchwald-Hartwig)
retrons.notes: Pd/bulky phosphine (BINAP, XPhos, DavePhos). Base: Cs2CO3, NaOtBu. Works for primary amines (→ secondary arylamines) and secondary amines (→ tertiary). Cu-based Ullmann conditions available as Pd-free alternative (higher T).

retrons.name: alpha_amino_reductive_amination
retrons.description: Amine ← aldehyde/ketone + amine + reductant (reductive amination)
retrons.notes: NaBH3CN or NaBH(OAc)3 in MeOH or DCE. For ketones: molecular sieves + NaBH3CN. Leuckart-Wallach: formic acid/formamide (no reductant). Chiral: asymmetric transfer hydrogenation with Ir/Rh catalyst.

retrons.name: aryl_amine_ullmann
retrons.description: Diaryl amine ← two aryl halides + amine/ammonia (Ullmann C–N)
retrons.notes: Cu catalysis (CuI, Cu2O). Higher temperature than Buchwald. Ligand acceleration: 1,10-phenanthroline, DMEDA. Suitable when Pd-free desired.

retrons.name: amide_direct
retrons.description: Amide ← carboxylic acid + amine (amide bond formation)
retrons.notes: DCC/DMAP, HATU/HOAt, EDC/HOBt, or T3P coupling reagents. Acyl chloride + amine (Schotten-Baumann) for scale-up. Watch for epimerization at α-chiral center. HATU preferred for hindered or acid-sensitive substrates.

retrons.name: nitrile_reduction_amine
retrons.description: Primary amine ← nitrile + reductant (nitrile reduction)
retrons.notes: LiAlH4 (THF, 0°C→rt), BH3·THF, or H2/Raney Ni. DIBAL-H gives imine intermediate (can be trapped). Watch for over-reduction to secondary amine with LAH.

retrons.name: aryl_ether_ullmann_o
retrons.description: Aryl ether ← aryl halide + alcohol/phenol (Ullmann O-arylation)
retrons.notes: Cu or Pd catalysis. For phenols: K2CO3 base, DMF. Chan-Lam coupling (Cu/O2, boronic acid + alcohol) at room temperature. Pd/Xantphos for secondary alcohols.

retrons.name: williamson_ether
retrons.description: Dialkyl ether ← alkoxide + alkyl halide (Williamson synthesis)
retrons.notes: SN2 mechanism: requires primary or methyl electrophile. Base: NaH, K2CO3, Ag2O. Solvent: DMF, THF. Elimination competes with secondary/tertiary electrophiles.

retrons.name: mitsunobu_inversion
retrons.description: Ether/ester with inversion ← alcohol + acidic partner + PPh3/DIAD
retrons.notes: Inverts stereochemistry at secondary alcohols. DEAD or DIAD + PPh3. Partners: carboxylic acids, phenols, sulfonamides, azides. Byproduct: Ph3P=O. Use DEAD-free protocols (cyanomethylene phosphoranes) for scale.

retrons.name: ester_from_acid_alcohol
retrons.description: Ester ← carboxylic acid + alcohol (Fischer esterification or coupling)
retrons.notes: Fischer esterification: H2SO4 or HCl catalyst, reflux, Dean-Stark. DCC/DMAP or coupling reagents for sensitive substrates. Acyl chloride + alcohol (Et3N, DMAP) for scale. Enzymatic esterification for stereoselective.

retrons.name: epoxide_from_alkene
retrons.description: Epoxide ← alkene (epoxidation)
retrons.notes: mCPBA in DCM for unfunctionalized alkenes. Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation (Ti/tartrate) for allylic alcohols. Jacobsen Mn-salen for non-allylic alkenes. Dimethyldioxirane (DMDO) for sensitive substrates.

retrons.name: ketone_from_friedel_crafts
retrons.description: Aryl ketone ← aromatic + acyl halide/anhydride (Friedel-Crafts)
retrons.notes: AlCl3 Lewis acid (1.1+ equiv). Works well for electron-rich arenes. Deactivated by EWG. Fries rearrangement alternative for phenol esters. Haworth synthesis for naphthalene/anthracene derivatives.

retrons.name: aldehyde_from_oxidation
retrons.description: Aldehyde ← primary alcohol (selective oxidation)
retrons.notes: Swern oxidation (oxalyl chloride, DMSO, Et3N, −78°C): mild, no over-oxidation. Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP): excellent for sensitive substrates. TEMPO/NaOCl for aqueous conditions. PCC or PDC in DCM for general use.

retrons.name: ketone_from_oxidation
retrons.description: Ketone ← secondary alcohol (oxidation)
retrons.notes: PCC, PDC, Swern, DMP, TEMPO, Oppenauer. Highly reliable and straightforward. Selectfluor/NaBr in MeCN/H2O also works (see notes).

retrons.name: carboxylic_acid_from_nitrile
retrons.description: Carboxylic acid ← nitrile (hydrolysis) or primary alcohol (oxidation)
retrons.notes: Nitrile hydrolysis: H2SO4/H2O reflux or NaOH/H2O2. Selective: partial hydrolysis to amide with H2O2/KOH. Permanganate or Jones oxidation of primary alcohols for acid.

retrons.name: cyclohexene_diels_alder
retrons.description: Cyclohexene ← diene + dienophile (Diels-Alder [4+2])
retrons.notes: Concerted [4+2] cycloaddition. endo/exo selectivity by geometry. Lewis acid catalysis (BF3, Et2AlCl) accelerates and improves endo selectivity. Asymmetric: Evans auxiliaries, chiral Lewis acids. Intramolecular DA for polycyclic targets.

retrons.name: cyclopropane_simmons_smith
retrons.description: Cyclopropane ← alkene + carbenoid (Simmons-Smith)
retrons.notes: IZnCH2I (from Et2Zn + CH2I2 or Zn + CH2I2). Syn addition, directed by adjacent OH groups. Alternative: Corey-Chaykovsky (sulfonium ylide) for terminal epoxides → cyclopropanes.

retrons.name: cyclopentane_pauson_khand
retrons.description: Cyclopentenone ← enyne (Pauson-Khand [2+2+1])
retrons.notes: Co2(CO)8 mediated. Intramolecular preferred. NMO or TMANO as promoter. Asymmetric PKR with chiral Co complexes.

retrons.name: lactam_ring_closure
retrons.description: Lactam ← amino acid or amino ester (intramolecular amide coupling)
retrons.notes: Intramolecular amide bond formation. Ring size determines strategy: 5-membered (γ-lactam) is easiest. β-lactam: Staudinger ([2+2]), ketene + imine. High-dilution or slow addition conditions for macrolactams.

retrons.name: heterocycle_buchwald_n_arylation
retrons.description: N-aryl heterocycle ← heteroaryl halide + N-H heterocycle (N-arylation)
retrons.notes: Pd/XPhos or Cu/phenanthroline catalysis. Pyrazoles, imidazoles, pyrroles, indoles are compatible. Chan-Lam (Cu/O2, boronic acid) at room temperature.

retrons.name: macrocycle_rce
retrons.description: Macrocyclic or medium-ring alkene ← diene (ring-closing metathesis)
retrons.notes: Grubbs 2nd gen or Hoveyda-Grubbs catalyst. High-dilution conditions for macrocycles. Ethylene gas evolution drives reaction. E/Z selectivity challenging. Cl2CH2 or toluene solvent.

retrons.name: alcohol_from_reduction
retrons.description: Alcohol ← carbonyl compound (reduction)
retrons.notes: NaBH4 (MeOH, 0°C→rt) for aldehydes/ketones. LiAlH4 for esters and amides. DIBAL-H for selective reduction (ester → aldehyde at −78°C). Asymmetric: CBS reduction (Corey-Bakshi-Shibata) with BH3·Me2S.

retrons.name: amine_from_reduction
retrons.description: Amine ← imine or nitro compound (reduction)
retrons.notes: NaBH4 or NaBH3CN for imines. H2/Pd-C for nitro → amine (transfer hydrogenation also works). Zn/AcOH for selective partial reduction of nitro groups. Asymmetric imine reduction: Ir(I)/chiral phosphine.

retrons.name: alkene_sharpless
retrons.description: 1,2-Diol ← alkene (dihydroxylation)
retrons.notes: OsO4 (cat., NMO as reoxidant, Upjohn). syn addition. Sharpless AD (AD-mix-α or β): asymmetric with DHQD or DHQ ligands. KMnO4 (basic): syn-diol but over-oxidation risk.

retrons.name: boc_protected_amine
retrons.description: Boc-amine ← free amine + Boc2O (protection)
retrons.notes: Boc2O, Et3N or DMAP, DCM. Removed by TFA (DCM) or HCl (dioxane). Orthogonal to Cbz (H2/Pd) and Fmoc (piperidine).

retrons.name: cbz_protected_amine
retrons.description: Cbz-amine ← free amine + benzyl chloroformate (Cbz-Cl)
retrons.notes: CbzCl, Et3N, DCM. Removed by H2/Pd-C (hydrogenolysis). Stable to TFA conditions (cf. Boc). Useful for orthogonal protection.

retrons.name: silyl_ether_protection
retrons.description: TMS/TBS/TIPS silyl ether ← alcohol + silyl chloride
retrons.notes: TBSCl/imidazole/DMF (most common). TIPS for sensitive substrates. TMS for temporary protection. Removed by TBAF (THF) or HF·pyridine. Selectivity: primary > secondary; less hindered > more hindered.

retrons.name: aryl_fluorine_snarf
retrons.description: Aryl fluoride ← aryl halide + F– (SNAr) or Balz-Schiemann
retrons.notes: SNAr requires strong EWG (NO2, CF3). KF or CsF, polar aprotic. Balz-Schiemann: diazonium tetrafluoroborate → pyrolysis. Pd-catalyzed fluorination (Pd/BrettPhos + Et3N·HF) for wider scope.

retrons.name: aryl_chloride_electrophilic
retrons.description: Aryl chloride ← arene + Cl2/electrophilic Cl source (EAS)
retrons.notes: Cl2/AlCl3, NCS (N-chlorosuccinimide)/Lewis acid, or SO2Cl2. Electron-rich arenes react well. Regioselectivity determined by existing substituents.

retrons.name: aryl_bromide_electrophilic
retrons.description: Aryl bromide ← arene + Br2 or NBS (EAS)
retrons.notes: Br2/FeBr3 or NBS in DCM/H2O. NBS preferred for electron-rich arenes (mild, selective). Regioselectivity driven by existing substituents (o/p directors).

retrons.name: allylic_bromination
retrons.description: Allylic bromide ← alkene + NBS (radical allylic bromination)
retrons.notes: NBS, benzoyl peroxide or hν, CCl4. Wohl-Ziegler conditions. Allylic radical is resonance-stabilized. Mixture of regioisomers possible with unsymmetric alkenes.

retrons.name: benzylic_bromination
retrons.description: Benzyl bromide ← toluene + NBS (radical benzylic bromination)
retrons.notes: NBS, AIBN or hν, CCl4. High selectivity for benzylic position. Used to access benzyl electrophiles for further reactions.

retrons.name: aryl_boronic_acid_miyaura
retrons.description: Arylboronic acid ← aryl halide + B2pin2 (Miyaura borylation)
retrons.notes: Pd(dppf)Cl2, B2pin2, KOAc, dioxane, 80°C. Alternative to arylboron reagents from ArMgX + B(OEt)3. Pin boronate can be hydrolyzed to boronic acid with NaIO4 or H2O2/NaOH.

retrons.name: vinyl_triflate_from_ketone
retrons.description: Vinyl triflate ← ketone + Tf2O or N-phenyltriflimide (via enolate)
retrons.notes: LDA → enolate → Tf2O or PhNTf2, THF, −78°C. Regioselective: kinetic (LDA, −78°C) vs thermodynamic (Et3N/PhNTf2). Used as aryl halide surrogate in cross-coupling.

retrons.name: organotrifluoroborate_from_halide
retrons.description: Potassium aryl/vinyl trifluoroborate ← halide + B2pin2 then KHF2
retrons.notes: Pd-catalyzed borylation then KHF2 precipitation. BF3K salts are air/moisture-stable alternatives to boronic acids. Direct coupling via Suzuki-Miyaura with Pd/base.

retrons.name: c_h_functionalization_direct
retrons.description: C–C bond via C–H activation ← arene + coupling partner
retrons.notes: Pd, Rh, Ir, or Ru catalysis. Directing group (DG) required for selectivity. CMD mechanism (acetate base, CMD conditions). Intramolecular C–H arylation for fused rings. Challenging: typically high T, specialized ligands.

retrons.name: sn2_alkyl_amine
retrons.description: N-alkylated amine ← amine + alkyl halide (SN2 N-alkylation)
retrons.notes: K2CO3 in DMF or MeCN. Primary alkyl halides only (Br/I preferred). Over-alkylation is a major concern: use excess amine or Mitsunobu. Gabriel synthesis (phthalimide → phthalimide alkylation → hydrazine deprotection) for primary amines without over-alkylation.

retrons.name: lactone_from_hydroxy_acid
retrons.description: Lactone ← hydroxy acid (intramolecular esterification)
retrons.notes: 5- and 6-membered lactones form readily (DCC or acid catalyst). Macrolactonization: high dilution, Yamaguchi, Corey-Nicolaou, or Shiina conditions. Enzymatic (lipase) for asymmetric.

retrons.name: sulfonamide_formation
retrons.description: Sulfonamide ← amine + sulfonyl chloride
retrons.notes: Et3N or pyridine in DCM. Very reliable. Sulfonyl chlorides can be made from sulfonic acids + PCl5 or SOCl2. Sulfonamides as NH-acid: can be deprotonated (pKa ~10) and alkylated.
